alerts.title: Probable Hypothyroidism Under-Treated and Levothyroxine Adherence Problem
alerts.message: Patient on levothyroxine 50 mcg with TSH 12.4 mIU/L (target below 4.5) and low free T4, with clinical hypothyroid features (fatigue, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, periorbital puffiness, delayed reflex relaxation). The plan states to continue levothyroxine 50 mcg unchanged, without addressing the elevated TSH. The patient reports often forgetting the thyroid tablet, which likely contributes to inadequate replacement. Weight gain may partly reflect hypothyroidism rather than the ART regimen alone. Guideline excerpts supplied do not contain specific levothyroxine dosing thresholds, so dose adjustment should follow standard thyroid management guidance.

evidence.recommended_action: Address adherence barriers and review levothyroxine dose in light of TSH 12.4 mIU/L and low free T4 before attributing weight gain to DTG; reassess thyroid function after dose adjustment.

alerts.title: Proposed DTG Switch for Weight Gain Not Supported by Current Evidence
alerts.message: Guidelines state that DTG-associated weight gain is not considered causal; the association may reflect less metabolic toxicity than older ART regimens. Weight gain of about 9 kg (BMI 33) is documented, but hypothyroidism is an unaddressed alternative explanation. Abnormal weight gain is listed as a recognised DTG adverse effect in the adverse-event reporting form, so it should be recorded and evaluated, though switching is not automatically indicated. Viral load was suppressed (<50 copies/mL) on 2025-11-10.

evidence.recommended_action: Do not switch DTG solely for weight gain before correcting hypothyroidism; document as possible adverse event and reassess weight after thyroid optimisation; if switching is considered, check viral load and adherence first.

alerts.title: Hyperglycaemia Risk Screening Needed on DTG
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend assessing hyperglycaemia risk for experienced clients transitioning to DTG; risk factors include age 30 or over and BMI 25 or more. This patient is 45 years old with BMI 33, so she has at least two risk factors. Fasting glucose today is 5.6 mmol/L, and the excerpts do not provide a confirmatory diagnostic threshold, so the result requires follow-up glucose assessment per the screening flowchart.

evidence.recommended_action: Complete hyperglycaemia screening per the DTG flowchart (check glucose as indicated by risk factors) and document the result; no such assessment is recorded in today's plan.
